text: When you build a REST API, good design makes your service easy to use. Start by giving your endpoints clear, simple names, such as /users or /orders. Use the right HTTP methods: GET to read data, POST to create it, and so on. Always return proper status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is not found. Good documentation helps other developers understand how your API works, so keep it clear and up to date. Finally, plan for versioning, for example /v1/users, so you can improve your API without breaking existing applications. These practices save time and prevent confusion.
